description:
Who we are  

 Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

 Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

 Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

 This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

 We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

 If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

  

 About the role  

 As a Member of Technical Staff focused on Applied AI, you will help shape how advanced machine learning capabilities are developed, adapted, and deployed across Atoms' physical AI systems.

 You will work at the intersection of AI research and real-world engineering, translating advances in foundation models, multimodal learning, perception, and embodied intelligence into systems capable of operating in complex, dynamic physical environments.

 This is not simply a role focused on integrating existing models or optimizing established machine learning pipelines. You will have the opportunity to develop novel approaches, influence model architectures, and solve challenging problems where existing methods may not be sufficient.

 You will work closely with researchers, machine learning engineers, robotics specialists, and autonomy teams to bridge the gap between emerging AI capabilities and their application to intelligent machines.

 This is a deeply technical, hands-on individual contributor role with significant influence over Atoms' AI architecture and technical direction.

  

 What you'll do 

 
 Design, develop, and apply advanced machine learning models to challenging problems in robotics, autonomy, and physical AI.

 Adapt and extend foundation models, multimodal architectures, and emerging AI techniques for real-world applications.

 Develop machine learning systems that process and reason over inputs such as video, images, LiDAR, radar, spatial information, and other sensor data.

 Advance approaches to perception, scene understanding, multimodal fusion, and learned representations of physical environments.

 Explore how world models, vision-language models, and action models can be applied to real-world decision-making and autonomous behavior.

 Develop novel training, fine-tuning, and adaptation strategies using large-scale real-world and simulated datasets.

 Improve model robustness, generalization, reliability, and performance across diverse operating conditions.

 Design evaluation methodologies that connect model performance to measurable improvements in real-world system behavior.

 Make architectural decisions spanning data, model design, training, evaluation, optimization, inference, and deployment.

 Collaborate with ML infrastructure and engineering teams to scale experimentation, training, and deployment.

 Translate research prototypes into reliable, efficient machine learning systems capable of operating under real-world compute, latency, and operational constraints.

 Identify opportunities where emerging research can materially improve existing or future AI capabilities.

 Provide technical leadership through hands-on development, architecture reviews, mentorship, and cross-functional collaboration.

 Help establish the technical standards and engineering practices for Atoms' growing AI organization.

 
  

 What we're looking for 

 
 Deep expertise in machine learning, with demonstrated experience developing sophisticated AI models or systems.

 Strong understanding of modern deep learning architectures and their application to computer vision, multimodal learning, robotics, autonomous systems, or related domains.

 Experience developing, adapting, or optimizing machine learning models for complex real-world applications.

 Experience with one or more areas such as perception, multimodal foundation models, representation learning, embodied AI, world models, or learned planning.

 Strong understanding of the full machine learning lifecycle, including data strategy, model architecture, training, evaluation, optimization, and inference.

 Experience working with large-scale datasets and building robust evaluation methodologies.

 Strong software engineering fundamentals and hands-on proficiency in Python, PyTorch, or comparable machine learning frameworks.

 Experience working across research and engineering disciplines to bring advanced ML capabilities into functioning systems.

 Demonstrated ability to make consequential technical decisions and influence engineering direction beyond individual projects.

 Ability to navigate ambiguous technical problems, develop solutions independently, and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

 
 Relevant experience 

 We are particularly interested in people who have worked on challenging problems within areas such as:

 
 Applied machine learning and physical AI

 Autonomous vehicles and autonomous systems

 Robotics and embodied intelligence

 Computer vision and multimodal perception

 Foundation model adaptation and fine-tuning

 Vision-language and vision-language-action models

 World models and representation learning

 Reinforcement learning and imitation learning

 Large-scale model training and evaluation

 Real-world deployment of machine learning systems

 
  

 Why join us 

 At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

  

 What else you need to know 

 This role is based in our San Francisco   office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

 Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 

 The base salary range for this role is $273,000 - $321,000 per year. 

 Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

 Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package. You may also be eligible for equity awards.

 Benefits Summary (USA Full-Time Exempt Employees): 

 
 Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, and Life Insurance

 Flexible Spending Account / Health Savings Account Options

 401(k)

 Equity

 Sick Time, Unlimited Flexible Time Off, and Paid Holidays

 Paid Parental Leave 

 Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit Plan

 
 Benefits are subject to change at the company's discretion.
Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

  

 Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?  

 #LI-Onsite
